newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance starts CEO search.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance starts CEO search.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co has started searching for a replacement for current chief executive officer William Brandt Jr., a turnaround and bankruptcy expert brought in in the wake of financial irregularities at the sub-prime auto financing company.
No timetable has been set for the search by executive recruiting firm Heidrick & Struggles Inc., a Mercury Finance spokesman said Tuesday.
"Just knowing what Bill does for a living, nobody assumed he'd be a permanent CEO," the spokesman said.

Brandt became chief executive officer in February, replacing John Brincat, who resigned shortly after the company said it would have to cut previously reported earnings for the past four years by about $90 million due to accounting irregularities.

The company, which is facing a federal probe and several shareholder lawsuits, has yet to report the amended earnings. The company did report a loss of $33.2 million, or $0.19 a share Monday for the first quarter of 1997. That loss included a $28.5 million loss from the sale of the company's Lyndon Insurance Group.
Mercury shares were down 1/16 at 2-1/4 Tuesday.
